title: Accountant II
description: MAIN PURPOSE OF THE JOB The Accountant is responsible for the overall financial support including field support during trainings/workshops by ensuring all financial transactions follow MSH financial policies and procedures and donor regulations. She/he will ensure financial documents submitted for review are complete, applicable taxes are deducted for financial transaction settlement, compiles payment sheet details during training for urgent financial settlement and follows up on timely settlement of taxes. S/he will also support the finance unit during audit process. SPECIFIC RESPONSIBILITY Support Country Finance Management Make sure that all financial documents (JVs, PVs, and Deposit vouchers) and any related documents are reviewed and shared with the finance coordinator for proper filing. Ensure all submitted MSH and sub contractor financial documents are complete and accurate and process cover payment documentation for approvals. Payment processing Ensure all financial documents are properly sequenced, have the applicable payment details attached for supervisors review and approvals. Ensure all financial documents have the required supporting documentation and all supporting documents are clear and original. Ensure receipts attached with payment documents are legally acceptable and have attachments as required. Ensure timely settlement of outstanding work and staff advances including sub contractor staff advances. Support with the review of sub contract invoices and consultant invoices. Training support Support during trainings/workshops for registration/attendance sheet recording and support with perdiem settlement preparation. Ensure applicable documentations are collected for urgent settlement. Support with audit process and organizing documents for audit and compliance review. Assist in the preparation of smooth conduct of internal and external audits. Qualifications REQUIRED MINIMUM EDUCATION Bachelor’s degree or Master’s Degree in accounting, Finance, Business management, or related field from a recognized university Required Minimum Experience Previous experience in USG-funded projects of similar nature, and good knowledge of USG rules and regulations. Experience in working and reviewing partners and sub contractors/grant documents is an advantage. Knowledge And Skills Oversee the overall financial activities of the project and ensure that activities comply with MSH Policies and procedures and with USG donor rules and regulations and statutory obligations including contractual requirements. Prepare payment vouches, cash receipts vouchers, and journal vouchers in accordance with MSH policies and procedures. Ensure all transactions have the necessary approvals, are accurately coded and charged to the right expenditure type, with appropriate documentation, and recorded into the QuickBooks database. Laise with central level technical advisors and regional managers for timely preparation and submission of monthly fund requests. Follow the timely settlement of outstanding work and staff advances and prepare an aging analysis report to be submitted to the MSH home office monthly. Prepare check payments, bank transfers, and bank letters in the name of the authorized payees/vendors as necessary. Review petty cash payments and replenishment requests to ensure they are in line with MSH Ethiopia’s petty cash policies. Prepare monthly payroll benefits, process timely payments based on MSH and donor applicable procedures. Responsible for workshop/training or similar event registration and attendance sheet follow up, compilation of payment sheet for urgent settlement by collecting accurate bank data and supporting documentation. Assist in the preparation of provident fund and government payables (withholding tax, income tax, pension) and make sure such payables are paid to the applicable authority office in time. Compile and process monthly VAT claims for a refund from the DoS as applicable. Assist in the preparation and smooth conduct of internal and external audit. MSH is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other protected category under applicable federal, state, and local laws. MSH complies with Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act, Section 4212 of the Vietnam Era Readjustment Assistance Act, as amended, and all related applicable regulations. title: Finance and Administrative Officer
description: I. TechnoServe Background Everyone deserves the opportunity to build a better future. This simple idea has been at the heart of TechnoServe’s work around the world for over 50 years. TechnoServe is a pioneer in leveraging the power of business and markets to create sustainable pathways out of poverty. The low-income communities in which we work are full of enterprising people. Their small-scale farms and businesses are the keys to economic development. But they face many challenges: low literacy, lack of access to jobs and markets, unpredictable political dynamics and, increasingly, the effects of climate change. For many women and young people, the challenges are even more daunting. Working with TechnoServe staff, people around the world are lifting themselves out of poverty. The results are amazing. When incomes increase and living conditions for families get better, they are able to access health care and education previously out of reach. Communities and even whole countries are better off. II. Position Description The Finance & Admin Officer is responsible for overseeing all financial management, accounting controls, and general office administration for the field project. This position maintains strict accounting practices and internal controls to ensure accurate financial reporting, compliance with donor standards, and proper administrative oversight. To maintain proper Segregation of Duties within a small project office environment, the Finance & Admin Officer serves as the primary verifier and reviewer for financial and administrative requests, while physical handling of cash, inventory custody, and initial log maintenance are assigned to the Administrative Assistant. III. Key Duties & Responsibilities Financial Management & Internal Controls Review & Verification: Check and verify all payment requests, purchase orders, invoices, and expense claims for accuracy, proper authorization, and budget availability before processing or payment initiation. Accounting & Data Entry Review: Review voucher coding, verify supporting documentation, and oversee accurate posting in the financial system. Ensure timely submission of financial returns to the main office. Bank & Financial Reconciliations: Perform monthly bank reconciliations, monitor cash flow, and ensure all advance accounts (staff/petty cash) are reconciled and cleared systematically. Compliance & Audit: Ensure strict adherence to TechnoServe policies, Ethiopian tax and labor laws, and donor financial regulations. Prepare for and support internal/external audits. Budget Oversight: Monitor project spending against approved budgets and alert the Program Manager to any variances or compliance risks. Syllogist / Microsoft Dynamics Workflows: Review purchase requisitions, orders, fund/award codes in the system, and specific fortnightly financial return deadlines. Administrative & Supervisory Oversight Direct Supervision: Supervise the Administrative Assistant, drivers, and support staff. Delegate duties, conduct performance reviews, and ensure tasks are completed in a timely manner. Segregation of Duty Enforcement: Maintain oversight over physical inventory, store custody, and petty cash operations managed by the Administrative Assistant. Perform random cash counts and periodic physical asset audits. Procurement Approval & Quality Control: Review procurement paperwork and verify that delivered goods and services match the requested quality and quantity prior to final payment authorization. Fleet & Logistics Monitoring: Review vehicle logbooks, fuel efficiency analysis, and logistics reports prepared by the Administrative Assistant or logistics staff. Timekeeping & Payroll Support: Oversee and approve monthly staff timesheet collections for field personnel and submit them to the country office. Audit and Compliance Assist the Accounts Manager and Senior Financial Controller and engage with auditors on project audits and tax hygiene audits. Assist the country office admin team with any finance-administrative cross-cutting matters. Undertake other related work as directed by the Controller or the Accounts Manager. Contact individuals or entities with delinquent accounts for clearance. Orient, train, motivate, and coach employees reporting to this position. IV. Required Skills And Experience Education: Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or Business Administration. Experience: Minimum of 4 years (or Master’s degree with 2 years) of progressive experience in financial management and accounting, preferably within an INGO environment. Technical Knowledge: Sound knowledge of IPSAS (International Public Sector Accounting Standards), Ethiopian tax/labor laws, and accounting software (Microsoft Dynamics - Syllogist). Excellent skills in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc. Supervisory Skills: Demonstrated ability to manage and mentor support staff. title: Surgeon
organization: Bete Markos Medical Surgical Center ,Debre Markos University and  Referral Hospital
description: Company Description Bete Markos Medical Surgical Center, Debre Markos University, and Referral Hospital form a collaborative healthcare and academic environment serving the Debre Markos community and surrounding regions. The institutions focus on delivering comprehensive medical and surgical care while supporting education, training, and research in a range of clinical disciplines. As a referral center, the hospital manages complex cases and provides specialized services to patients from diverse backgrounds. Team members work within a multidisciplinary setting that values clinical excellence, ethical practice, and continuous professional development. Role Description This is a full-time, on-site Surgeon role based in Debre Markos. The Surgeon will provide preoperative assessments, perform surgical procedures, and manage postoperative care for patients with a variety of conditions. Day-to-day responsibilities include conducting clinical examinations, reviewing diagnostic tests, developing treatment plans, and collaborating with anesthesiology, nursing, and other medical teams to ensure safe and effective patient care. The role also involves participating in ward rounds, outpatient clinics, and emergency surgical services, while maintaining accurate medical records and adhering to hospital protocols and safety standards. The Surgeon may contribute to teaching and mentoring medical students, residents, and other healthcare professionals, and is encouraged to participate in quality improvement and professional development activities. Qualifications Strong foundation in general Medicine and core surgical principles, with the ability to manage diverse clinical presentations. Proficiency in Surgery, including operative techniques, perioperative management, and evidence-based clinical decision-making. Experience or training in Orthopedic Surgery for musculoskeletal and trauma-related procedures is highly beneficial. Experience or training in Plastic Surgery for reconstructive and soft-tissue procedures is an advantage. Exposure to or interest in Ophthalmology for basic ocular assessments and coordination with eye-care specialists is desirable. Recognized medical degree, completed surgical residency or equivalent specialized training, and valid professional licensure/registration. Commitment to patient-centered care, ethical practice, and adherence to safety and infection-prevention standards. Ability to work effectively within multidisciplinary teams, with strong communication, clinical documentation, and time-management skills. Willingness to participate in teaching, mentoring, and ongoing professional development, including training in a university-affiliated setting.
